title: Preserve registered verifier failure under inherited interactive inspection
body:
A failing registered verifier could print `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` when the environment contained `PYTHONINSPECT=1`: after the exception Python entered a REPL, and ordinary terminal EOF returned success. Remove that ambient setting from the existing copied child environment in the shared launch path.

The change preserves stdin, explicit manifest flags including `-i` and `-O`, and the running parent's environment. File, module and command-string replay, optional dependency installation and the Windows ownership gate use that shared boundary. This does not constrain deliberately interactive/hostile verifiers or repair an already-running outer interpreter started in inspection mode. No frozen pins, selected metadata or mathematical claims change.

## Validation

On macOS27.0 arm64, CPython3.12.7, Git2.44.0:

- Six real-terminal/environment methods reproduce ten failing assertions/subtests before the fix and pass after it in normal and optimized modes. The generated registered-package fixture raises a real exception; terminal EOF cannot produce PASS after the fix. File/`-m`/`-c`, stdin input, descendant inheritance, unchanged parent environment and explicit `-i` are covered.
- Forty compatibility methods run in each mode:32 pass,8 native-Windows cases skip. Coverage includes onboarding PackageTests, private bytecode isolation, POSIX termination and Windows Job Object tests. Native Windows execution is unrun; the portable dispatch control only checks the environment/argv passed to its gate.
- An exact four-file committed archive passes all six new methods in both modes from a read-only source directory without `.git`; bytes remain unchanged. Git remains available for disposable fixture repositories. Removing only the new environment removal in a separate cold copy makes the optimized registered regression fail again.
- No full archive or scientific replay was run. Historical packages that pin an older shared runner as a live input may reject source drift; these targeted passes are not claims that all historical replays pass.

Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19143425

Base `20a1e31bc6009b9b3f4d084bbaadc6350e34fcba`; head `a7d680618e5b4816dd6e51841c2f5a8027ebc0b3`. Two commits: independent failure controls, then scoped launch policy/documentation. Exact committed closure SHA256 `30634afa8a1402ce81196e6ed9b63604f628343604ee44c22e0f5ed4f6a40f83`.

Prepared by JoyboyBrian with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Retains Douglas Colkitt's shared runner/generator and existing contributors' environment, cache and process-ownership work. Open next question: native Windows terminal corroboration; broader startup/dependency isolation requires a separate contract.
